stem:
The diagram shows Tejas's arrangement of one cell and a small lamp. One copper wire joins the lamp to the positive terminal. There is a gap at G, so no wire joins the lamp to the negative terminal.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: The lamp does not glow, because the gap at G leaves the path incomplete.
The lamp glows, because one wire already joins the lamp to the positive terminal.
The lamp glows only if the gap at G is beside the positive terminal, even when no wire completes the path.
The lamp glows whenever it sits near the cell, even with the gap at G.

teacher.key_rationale: A lamp glows only when wires complete a path from one cell terminal through the lamp to the other. The gap at G leaves that path incomplete, so the lamp does not glow.
teacher.figure_note: Cell and lamp with an open gap G in the return wire.
